To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HCN1 channel inhibition increases synaptic strength in a subset of entorhinal synaptic terminals by enhancing the rate of spontaneous and evoked exocytosis.

pre-synaptic hyperpolarization activated cyclic nucleotide-gating (HCN) channels reduce the rate, but not the amount, of exocytotic vesicle release from a subset of entorhinal cortical (EC) synaptic terminals and thereby constrain synaptic strength.
HCN1 pre-synaptic channels restrict the rate and extent of spontaneous and synchronous release at a subset of cortical terminals within the EC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how pre-synaptic channels, in addition to post-synaptic channels and receptors, affect synaptic transmission and how these channels are regulated.
how HCN1 channels modulate the release of the excitatory neurotransmitter, glutamine, at a specific cortical synapse, the EC-ECIII synapse.
understanding the role HCN1 channels in cortical synaptic transmission and plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCN1 channel activity reduces the rate of exo-cytosis from a sub-population of cortical synaptic terminals and thereby reduces the amount of neurotransmitter released from these terminals.
HCN1 channel activity in cortical synaptic terminals regulates the release of glutamate and therefore synaptic strength.
HCN1s are a novel regulator of the release probability of a subset of cortical synapses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCN1 channel activity at pre-synaptic terminals is a novel and important mechanism by which the strength of synaptic connections are regulated.
HCN1 channel inhibition increases the release of glutamate at a subset of cortical synapses in the EC and thereby enhances the rate of synaptic transmission.
the HCN1 channels reduce the release of glutamate from a subset of synaptic boutons within the entorhinal cortical network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HCN1 channel activity is required for normal release of glutamate from a subset of synaptic boutons within the EC.
HCN1 channel function is not only restricted to the dendrites but also plays a role at the synapse, which is a novel concept.
HCN1 channel expression within the pre-synaptic terminal of a subset of synaptic boutons within the cortex is important to regulate synaptic strength and plastic mechanisms.
